baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired forms of ح ل ل at words 5 and 25 frame repeated ح ر م protections and the later permission to hunt.
baseline_models.mechanism: The ayah organizes conduct as state transitions: protected signs, times, places, offerings, and travelers may not be prematurely unbound, while release from the protected state opens a bounded activity. Permission is therefore timed and relational rather than a permanent property of the hunted thing.

activation_trace.role: The image of a restriction dissolving links the initial ban on making protected things licit with the later transition out of restriction.
Prohibition and prevention supply the protected states through which the release sequence moves.
Seeking and taking what resists names the newly available activity whose timing remains regulated.

changed_reading.before: The ayah lists sacred prohibitions and then separately permits hunting.
changed_reading.after: The prohibitions and hunting permission form one gated order in which legal capacity changes with state, time, and location.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: شعائر, الهدي, القلائد, آمين البيت, يبتغون, and رضوان describe marked beings moving toward a protected destination for an acknowledged purpose.
baseline_models.mechanism: Signs, offerings, collars, direction, destination, and seeking combine into a legibility system. Visible markers and declared orientation carry protection along a route, extending sanctity from a fixed house to vulnerable travelers and offerings in motion.

activation_trace.role: A sign that makes ritual status perceptible supplies the public legibility of the protected movement.
The offering sent toward the sanctuary supplies a protected object whose status travels with it.
A neck-worn marker makes the offering's protected claim externally recognizable.
Purposeful orientation supplies the travelers' directed movement rather than mere presence near a site.
The dwelling or refuge supplies the destination around which the protected corridor is organized.
Active seeking supplies the travelers' intelligible purpose on the route.
Sought abundant approval gives the journey a non-hostile declared end.

changed_reading.before: The ayah protects a collection of sacred objects and pilgrims.
changed_reading.after: The ayah creates a mobile safe-passage regime in which visible markers, orientation, and purpose extend protection from sanctuary to route.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction joining يجرمنكم, شنآن, صدّوكم, تعتدوا, and the paired تعاونوا clauses blocks hatred from becoming transgression and redirects collective capacity.
baseline_models.mechanism: A remembered obstruction can generate hostile affect, hostile affect can drive boundary crossing, and cooperation can multiply either repair or harm. The ayah interrupts the first causal chain and routes shared agency toward expansive good and protective restraint rather than delayed good and aggression.

activation_trace.role: The image of acquiring or causing an outcome casts hatred as a possible producer of wrongful action.
Hatred and enmity supply the affective pressure that the prohibition refuses to treat as authorization.
Diversion and repulsion supply the remembered injury without determining the response.
Crossing a limit supplies the prohibited behavioral conversion of injury into retaliation.
Mutual assistance supplies a shared amplifier whose moral direction must be selected.
Expansive good and obedience supply the constructive channel for collective power.
A barrier against harm supplies the self-limiting protection that governs both cooperation and retaliation.
Delay from good identifies the disabling channel into which cooperation must not be routed.

changed_reading.before: The ayah commands fairness toward enemies and recommends helping in good deeds.
changed_reading.after: The ayah is an affect-to-action firewall: it prevents injury from authorizing retaliation and treats cooperation as an amplifier that must be deliberately routed.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding demand to complete binding agreements turns the focus ayah's repeated prohibitions into covenant maintenance. The collar is not only a ritual ornament: together with the knot and obligation images, it is a visible bearer of a social claim that others must honor rather than unbind.

activation_trace.role: Untying a knot supplies the focus prohibition's image of dissolving an established protection.
Placing an obligation on the neck supplies the marked offering as a carrier of binding responsibility.
Completion without deficiency makes protection of the focus ayah's marked parties an act of fulfilling rather than merely observing.
A firmly concluded covenant supplies the binding social relation that the visible marker externalizes.

structural_cues: 5:1 places fulfillment of agreements immediately before 5:2 and shares the ح ل ل state vocabulary.
The focus sequence moves from ritual signs to collars and directed travelers before it addresses retaliation and cooperation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies completion, binding agreements, untying, and a neck-borne obligation; I infer that visible ritual status externalizes a covenant others owe to the marked bearer. A live alternative is that 5:1 governs contracts generally while 5:2 begins an unrelated ritual list.

changed_reading.before: Visible sacred markers identify things that must not be disturbed.
changed_reading.after: Visible sacred markers carry enforceable relational claims, so disturbing the marked traveler or offering amounts to unbinding a covenant of protection.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later hunting rule fills out what happens after release: predatory capacity is trained, delegated, made to hold for another, and accompanied by articulated remembrance. Leaving a restricted state opens acquisition, but lawful agency remains disciplined at the point of capture.

activation_trace.role: Dissolution of restriction supplies the transition after which hunting becomes available.
Seeking and taking resistant prey supplies the released activity whose execution needs specification.
Knowledge made available through repeated teaching turns raw predatory force into instructed agency.
Hunting animals supply delegated capture rather than an unstructured human taking.
Holding and retaining supplies control at the decisive boundary between pursuit and usable acquisition.
Running the name on the tongue makes the capture explicitly accountable rather than merely successful.

structural_cues: 5:4 repeats ح ل ل twice and answers a question about what is permitted after 5:2's release-and-hunt transition.
Teaching occurs three times around the hunting animals, followed by holding, naming, protective restraint, and accounting.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies release, trained hunting agents, retained prey, and spoken remembrance; I infer that the later ayah operationalizes the focus permission as controlled delegated capture. A live alternative is that 5:4 regulates food separately and does not qualify the force of 5:2's hunting license.

changed_reading.before: Once the protected state ends, hunting is simply permitted.
changed_reading.after: Release restores activity but not unbounded predation: acquisition remains trained, controlled, attributable, and answerable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The near-verbatim return of hatred as a possible producer of wrongdoing moves the focus rule from physical trespass into testimony and judgment. The added scale, balance, repeated justice command, and proximity to protective restraint make hostile affect a test of calibration across action and adjudication.

activation_trace.role: Acquiring or producing an outcome supplies the causal hinge by which hatred could generate transgression.
Hatred supplies the pressure that must not set the response standard.
Boundary crossing supplies the focus ayah's first named failure mode under hostile affect.
Putting oneself within protection supplies the internal discipline paired with cooperative conduct.
A straight balance supplies a public standard that hostile feeling may not tilt.
The repeated causal hinge explicitly transfers the focus warning into the justice setting.
The repeated hatred term identifies the same affective input across both settings.
Justice in judgment and conduct supplies the positively repeated response to hatred.
Nearness supplies an explicit relation between calibrated justice and protective restraint.
Repeated self-protection closes the justice instruction as a discipline against affective distortion.

structural_cues: 5:8 repeats the rare يجرمنكم شنآن construction from 5:2 before replacing transgression with failure to act justly.
The sequence in 5:8 moves from public witness and balance to a doubled justice command and then to nearness to protective restraint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical repetition plus testimony, balance, justice, and nearness; I infer that 5:8 is an operational expansion of 5:2 from bodily or spatial retaliation to evidentiary and judicial calibration. A live alternative is that the two ayat are parallel exhortations without one specifying the other.

changed_reading.before: Do not answer exclusion from the sanctuary with aggressive retaliation.
changed_reading.after: The same anti-retaliation discipline governs evidence and judgment: hatred must alter neither another's access nor the measure used to assess them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The paired covenant accounts show hostility becoming durable when binding commitments are broken or neglected. One sequence answers breach with pardon and gracious turning aside; the next depicts forgotten obligation followed by induced enmity and hatred. The focus ayah's cooperation rule therefore controls whether collective memory interrupts injury or institutionalizes it.

activation_trace.role: Hatred and enmity supply the focus affect whose persistence the later covenant sequences explain.
Mutual assistance supplies the collective mechanism that can stabilize either repair or wrongdoing.
Undoing what was firmly built supplies the initiating covenant failure.
Leaving punishment and effacing fault supplies one non-recursive response to repeated breach.
Graciously turning aside from fault supplies a second way not to transmit breach into retaliation.
Neglecting and leaving aside a remembered share supplies the loss of a coordinating obligation.
Incitement supplies the directional move by which neglected obligation becomes active intergroup hostility.
Enmity supplies the social relation that hardens after covenantal forgetting.
Affective aversion supplies the internal counterpart to the external relation of enmity.

structural_cues: 5:13 and 5:14 are adjacent covenant-failure sequences that both include forgetting but display different response paths.
The focus ayah places positive and negative cooperation immediately after refusing hatred-driven transgression.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies covenant undoing, forgetting, pardon, gracious turning aside, incitement, enmity, and hatred; I infer a causal contrast between interrupting and reproducing covenantal injury. A live alternative is that the two later sequences only report distinct communal histories and do not model the focus cooperation commands.

changed_reading.before: The focus ayah restrains an immediate retaliatory impulse caused by a past obstruction.
changed_reading.after: The focus ayah also governs the long social afterlife of injury: shared practices can either metabolize breach through restraint or preserve it as organized enmity.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing movement sequence places sacred land, turning back, a gate, trust, refusal to act, renewed prohibition, and wandering around a contested threshold. This expands the focus protection of sanctuary-bound travelers into a reciprocal passage ethic: sacredness forbids hostile obstruction but also demands coordinated, non-paralyzed movement through a rightful entrance.

activation_trace.role: Purposeful orientation supplies the sanctuary-bound movement whose passage the focus ayah protects.
A dwelling or refuge supplies the protected destination.
Diversion and repulsion supply the wrongful denial of access that must not be mirrored.
A protected spatial precinct supplies the boundary whose meaning is tested by movement toward it.
Mutual assistance supplies the coordinated capacity needed to preserve or traverse the passage.
A purified place supplies a second sacred destination approached through commanded movement.
Returning or being turned back supplies the reversal that aborts directed access.
Turning one's back supplies embodied withdrawal from the commanded route.
An entrance supplies the specific threshold through which coordinated passage must occur.
Reliance supplies courage for action without making aggressive force the sole ground of entry.
Sitting out action supplies the collective paralysis opposed to directed passage.
Renewed prohibition supplies the consequence by which refused entry becomes prolonged exclusion.

structural_cues: 5:21 commands entry into sacred land and forbids turning back; 5:23 narrows action to entering a gate with trust.
5:24 answers with explicit refusal and sitting, while 5:26 pairs renewed prohibition with the branchless ت ي ه occurrence for wandering.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two sacred destinations, obstruction or reversal, a gate, coordinated counsel, refusal, sitting, prohibition, and wandering; I infer a reciprocal passage ethic in which sanctuary is protected by both non-obstruction and responsible movement. A live alternative is that the closing narrative concerns a distinct military entry and should not be mapped onto pilgrimage access.

changed_reading.before: The focus ayah protects people already traveling toward a sacred destination and forbids revenge for prior exclusion.
changed_reading.after: The focus ayah regulates a whole threshold system: do not block protected approach, do not turn sacred access into retaliation, and organize shared agency so fear does not collapse directed movement into exclusion or stasis.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the disease-transfer branch of ع د و is distant from the juridical sense of aggression. It remains anchored because ع د و occurs twice beside reciprocal cooperation in 5:2 and returns as social enmity after incitement in 5:14. Downstream prose should present transmission only as a network analogy for reproduced hostility, not as the lexical gloss of عدوان or as a medical claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two تعاونوا clauses make conduct transmissible through a group, while the split branch inventory for focus-root ع د و includes transfer of disease alongside aggression and enmity.

activation_trace.role: Mutual assistance supplies the contact network through which a disposition can be multiplied.
Transfer of disease supplies the deliberately branch-distant image of aggression propagating through social contact.
Hatred and enmity supply the affective load that the analogy treats as reproducible.
Incitement supplies an active mechanism that sets hostility moving between parties.
The same transfer image recasts enduring intergroup enmity as a propagated relation while remaining explicitly analogical.
Affective aversion supplies what is carried internally as enmity spreads socially.

changed_reading.before: Do not collaborate in sinful or aggressive acts.
changed_reading.after: Do not let cooperative networks become vectors through which injured hostility is transmitted, stabilized, and reproduced as new boundary crossing.

strongest_changes: The repeated 5:2 and 5:8 hatred construction turns anti-retaliation into a single standard governing access, testimony, and judgment.
5:1 makes marked ritual protection covenantal: the visible sign carries a binding claim that others must fulfill.
5:4 shows that release from restriction restores agency without removing training, control, naming, or accountability.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah became a threshold-and-network protocol rather than a flat rule list: it marks mobile claims, gates changing permissions, blocks hostile affect from setting standards, and directs collective power across sacred passage.
remaining_uncertainties: The covenant reading may overconnect 5:1's general agreements with the collars and ritual signs of 5:2.
The closing sacred-land narrative may illuminate passage structurally without directly specifying sanctuary access in 5:2.
The transmission outlier depends on a branch-distant image and must remain an explicit analogy.
